Think it through, considering your particular needs/whereabouts and conditions possible. Ok, first, determine what you are prepping for. You should always try to be prepared for the most likely SHTF sitation, which for most people is a loss of job or other personal disaster that could knock you down, but doesn't affect others in your area. I've known lots of preppers who have used their supplies just to survive the small things that life throws at you. Start with that scenario. It is the easiest to imagine. What would you need on hand to survive a total loss of income for 1-3 months? Cash for bills(this can be used for supplies later during a grid down scenario, at least for the first week or so), a simple water filter like life straw or a counter top filter, meal plan and stock up on the foods you usually eat(not LTS), stock up on toiletries/medications/cleaning supplies/other consumables.

Once you have that in hand, you can start in on the less likely, but possible SHTF scenarios, probably civil unrest leading to the break down of society. You would add your self defense to this list. I'm a chick, so I'm not super up on firearms knowledge, but I've approach it this way. It goes in order of what I can afford. Shotgun, Handgun, Rifle. I have the shotgun, working on the handgun now. I feel like alot of people go overboard on the self defense, but I'm a hobbit prepper, not a road warrior :P

In the scenario of a break down of society where you will see an interruption of most services that depend on, you will need to be prepared to provide those services: sanitation, medical care(within reason), drinking/cooking water, food, protection, shelter, warmth, etc.

Sanitation: Don't go buy a bunch of toilet paper. It is too bulky to store and if you have to run, too much precious space in your vehicle. Instead, order a peri bottle off amazon(search Medline Cleansing Bottle), every woman who has given birth knows what it is. We get them post-partum, it is essentially a hand held bidet. Then go to your local fabric store and get several yards of cotton flannel, cut into wipes. The peri bottle is to rinse and the wipes are to dry. Reusable, washable, much less space. I would suggest having two sets per person, one for drying and one for #2s. You can wash your hair with ACV and baking soda, but shampoo will be good for about 3 years in original bottle. Soap, toothpaste, etc. Post collapse, disease will be the biggest killer, not people with guns. Sanitation will be your first line of defense.

Water: I suggest getting a lifestraw for each member of your family. It can be used buggin in or out, very portable. After that, estimate your amount of consumed water in your household per day and get a counter top water filter that can filter that much. In an emergency, a water bob that fits in your tub will store a quick stash of water in your house that you can use while you get your feet under you.

Food: Your first couple months of storage should be food you usually eat. You don't want to shock your system by switching to LTS foods you don't normally eat. I've started making a list of all the foods we usually eat and then I break that down into the basic foods contained that recipe. For each basic food, I have researched the best methods for storing that food, within my budget. Canned foods are great for immediate consumption, but over time they lose nutrition and change in texture. Freeze dried is the best for LTS(long term storage) of several foods, like shredded cheese, fruits, meat. Pasta, grains, beans can be stored dry with O2 absorbers. The goal is to store food now with a long shelf life and no continuing energy requirements. This is all food you will eat when you have no way of getting more food. But once you have this all in hand, you should look toward learning food growing/harvesting/raising skills. Prepping is all good to keep you alive, but what happens when your food runs out? Do you know how to start generating your own food?

Medication: go to youtube and look up "Patriot Nurse". She has some great videos, I found her when I was looking for a list of medical supplies to store. I think there is a video on what to buy if you only have $100. Start there. If you have prescription medications, see if you can arrange with your doctor to buy a three month supply, do it. Pain meds, if you have kids, walk that aisle and imagine scenarios where you would need a particular med for them, rotate according to expire dates.

Shelter: Big question! Are you buggin in or bugging out? Have a plan for both! The people in California had to bug out, there were very few who tried to weather the fires at home, and many who did probably didn't make it. Plan what you will do in both scenarios and know what your trigger is for buggin out. If you are watching for that trigger, you will be ahead of the horde. If you have a stable BOL(bug out location), perhaps a like minded relative who has given you permission to flee to their home, see if you can pack in supplies to have there ready for you. That makes bugging out faster, as you don't have to pack up everything you need.

Energy: First, in a long term grid down situation or where utilities are spotty, you will need to pair down your electicity usage. Its all about energy conversions. You need to figure out how to transfer the activities/tools that use electrical energy to another form of energy(kinetic, thermal, chemical, mechanical, gravitational, etc.). Mechanical is big, so start looking for hand tools that replace electical tools. There is a saying in prepping circles, "Two is one, one is none". It means that you need to have multiples of items you use, because they can and will break and then you are SOL. I'm not discounting a solar setup, it is just very expensive per watt generated and it is dependant on weather conditions. Reducing your electrical energy consumption to the bare minimum and THEN getting a solar setup to match that need would be my suggestion.

I can't recommend survivalblog.com enough. Order the DVD/thumb drive of past articles and you will have a treasure trove of reading material on prepping/survival skills.
